rationale: Given the Chief Justice’s emphasis on a narrow, uniform rule under Patsy/Felder and his role as assigner, Roberts is the modal choice to write a consensus opinion reaffirming that state courts may not impose administrative-exhaustion prerequisites on § 1983 claims. The main risk of separate writings comes from Gorsuch/Thomas (Supremacy Clause and separation-of-powers framing) and Jackson/Sotomayor (practical harms and access-to-court emphasis), though the unanimity and clear precedent should keep concurrences limited.
